description: Multi-tenant isolation. A question that names a specific tenant filters its tenant-scoped tables by tenant_id. Questions that ask across tenants ("for each tenant", "all tenants") carry tenant=null and the gold does NOT add a filter.

Soft-delete default: unless a question says otherwise, soft-deleted rows (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are EXCLUDED from any table whose rows the question directly counts, lists or aggregates. Rule is NOT transitive to joined dimensions.
A row whose deleted_at IS NOT NULL. Explicitly requested only when a question asks for deleted rows.

sql: deleted_at IS NULL AND status IN ('active','past_due') AND (ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at > {as_of})
description: The broader glossary definition that adds the status filter and ended_at > as_of. Matches ONLY "active per the glossary" / the view. Plain English "active" uses `active_simple`.

sql: ended_at IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL
description: English "active" default on subscriptions: ended_at IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL, with no explicit status filter. Only "active subscription(s)" matches here — bare "active" on tenants or plans is a separate concept and is NOT this term. Use `active_subscription` when the question says "active per the glossary" or uses the view.
A row in billing.tax_rates with effective_to IS NULL. Historical rows are kept for audit; "current" means the one row per jurisdiction with effective_to IS NULL.

A row in billing.addresses with effective_to IS NULL. If a tenant has multiple effective_to IS NULL rows for a given address_id + tenant, the gold uses the greatest address_id as the winner (SCD2 tie-break). Gold never joins through the whole addresses table for "current".
An invoice whose status is 'overdue'. The generator sets this deterministically; the gold must NOT re-derive overdue from due_date.
status='paid' only. A question saying "paid or partial" uses `paid_or_partial` instead.

phrases: paid or partial;paid or partial invoices
description: status is paid or partial. The default revenue definition in this suite.
A plan on a monthly billing interval. Required when computing MRR; triggered also by the "MRR" / "monthly recurring revenue" phrases on the KPI side.

sql: issued_at >= DATE_TRUNC('month', CAST({as_of} AS DATE)) - INTERVAL '1' MONTH AND issued_at < DATE_TRUNC('month', CAST({as_of} AS DATE))
description: The previous calendar month in UTC relative to {as_of} — e.g. for as_of 2026-06-30, [2026-05-01, 2026-06-01). Trailing-30-days questions say so explicitly and do NOT use this term.
Difference ≤ N day boundaries crossed in UTC. "Within 7 days" does NOT mean a rolling 8-day window — it means difference ≤ 7.
Documentation only: a ratio with a zero denominator is NULL — not 0 and not an engine divide-by-zero error. Gold uses NULLIF or a HAVING/WHERE guard.

phrases: daily in the tenant's billing timezone;monthly in the tenant's billing timezone
description: Documentation only: gold converts UTC timestamps via AT TIME ZONE tenants.billing_timezone before truncating. DuckDB requires ICU; SQLite gold is null on DST zones for the affected periods.

phrases: refunds attached to invoices;credit transactions;promotion applications
description: Documentation only: refunds, credit_transactions and promotion_applications have no currency_code column. They are treated as denominated in the attached invoice's currency; refunds not attached to an invoice are USD. FX-converted to USD via the fx_conversion rule.

Documentation only: monthly/periodic buckets for refunds, credit transactions and promotion applications use the row's OWN date column (created_at / applied_at), NOT the attached invoice's issued_at, unless the question explicitly says so.

phrases: round down to integer;FLOOR to integer at innermost
description: Documentation only: monetary conversions and divisions FLOOR to integer at the innermost possible point (per-row, before aggregation). Ratios are expressed as integer per-mille (×1000, floor). "Average" questions say explicitly whether to round and at which stage. Gold never returns a float where an integer is sensible.

Documentation only: a question whose text asks for order carries ordered: true, and its gold ORDER BY includes a deterministic tie-break (usually the row's primary key ASC). Row-order matters only when ordered: true.
Documentation only: column names in a question are intent, not required output names. The validator compares row-sets by position, not by column label.

Documentation only: "For each X ..." / "per X ..." return one row per qualifying X, with 0 for count/SUM measures and NULL for other measures when nothing matches that X. "X that have ..." / "X with at least one ..." return only matching X.
Documentation only: value = rate_e8 / 1e8. Used by billing.exchange_rates.rate_e8.
Documentation only: percentage = pct_e6 / 1e6.
Documentation only: unit price in cents = unit_price_e4 / 1e4.
Documentation only: monetary values are stored in the currency's minor unit (cents for USD, paise for INR, etc.).
